newsitem.title: USA: Senate aide sees U.S. budget deal almost done.
newsitem.headline: Senate aide sees U.S. budget deal almost done.

text.p: The White House and Congress are nearing final agreement on a five-year plan to balance the federal budget and only a few minor issues remain to be resolved, a Senate Republican aide told reporters Thursday.
The aide said the White House was objecting to the Senate Budget Committee opening formal consideration of the budget as scheduled later in the day.
He said, "There are a couple of minor tweaks," that need to be made in the budget to meet Democratic concerns that need to be made before the closed-door negotiations can conclude.
Separately, Christina Martin, spokeswoman for House Speaker Newt Gingrich, said White House congressional budget talks had adjourned for the time being and would restart later this afternoon.
She said that there were still "small differences" and "fine details" to be worked out, but added that she was "quite optimistic" that the issues could be wrapped up.
